result.description:
Worrells is a fast growing, specialist accounting firm with expertise in solvency management and insolvency administration. We have carved a successful niche in the small to medium enterprise market by delivering quality service and processes with our unique systems. Established in 1973, Worrells now have 36 principals in 28 locations across NSW, QLD, ACT, VIC and WA, we draw upon broader resources and technical expertise enabling us to be focused locally while being resourced nationally.

We are looking for a full time Insolvency Accountant to join our NSW/ACT team based in Parramatta NSW. The successful candidate will be responsible for:

Day to day file management of insolvency appointments (from start to finish)
Preparation of statutory lodgements
Liaising with directors, employees, creditors, banks, statutory authorities and other stakeholders
Collection and investigation into records
Prioritise and manage workloads to meet conflicting deadlines
Analyse financial statements and diverse financial data
Drafting of reports and preparation of creditors meetings
Investigations into insolvent trading, voidable transactions and offences committed by officers
Attending sites to inspect, collect and record assets and books and records
Assisting with Fair Entitlements Guarantee claims and calculating employee entitlements.

We are seeking a candidate who has:

Proficient knowledge of Microsoft Office (Words, Excel, Outlook)
A Bachelor Degree or equivalent in Commerce, Finance or Accounting
Excellent communication skills (both written and verbal)
CA or CPA qualified (or willing to obtain)
ARITA Introduction to Insolvency certification
ARITA professional qualification (or willing to obtain)
Previous experience in insolvency is required.

We understand the importance of work-life balance, and we offer flexibility to support your needs. You'll become part of a collaborative team of professionals who are dedicated to both their work and personal growth. We provide opportunities for ongoing learning and development, and you'll have access to resources that will help you advance in your career. Worrells is committed to your professional growth, and we'll provide the support you need to succeed.

Adelaide, CBD

Part time, temporary 24-month position working 11.25 hours per week (backfill as required)

About the role

Join SA Pathology as a Domiciliary Support Officer and play an important role in coordinating domiciliary specimen collection services. Working both independently and as part of a supportive team, you will manage scheduling, maintain accurate records and provide administrative support to help ensure patients receive timely, high-quality care.

This is a varied role where you'll coordinate workloads, manage databases, communicate with patients and staff, and support the efficient day-to-day operation of the domiciliary phlebotomy service. Your organisation, attention to detail and commitment to customer service will help deliver a responsive and reliable service to the community.

About You

You are an organised and customer-focused professional who enjoys coordinating services and supporting both patients and colleagues.

- Communicate confidently with staff and patients

- Organise workloads and manage competing priorities

- Use Microsoft Office and databases confidently

- Deliver accurate administration and data entry

- Work independently and as part of a supportive team

About us

Statewide Clinical Support Services (SCSS) is a unique public healthcare organisation that serves health consumers and provides specialist clinical services to the health system in South Australia. SCSS encompasses BreastScreen SA, SA Dental, SA Medical Imaging, SA Pathology, and SA Pharmacy. Come and work with us to improve the health and well-being of South Australians, across all age groups and at any time of their life or health need. 

What we offer

Salary Benefits: Enjoy flexible salary packaging options, including up to $9,010 each FBT year for living expenses (such as mortgage, rent, utilities and groceries) plus an additional $2,650 for meal and entertainment expenses.

Annual Leave: Enjoy paid recreation leave for essential rejuvenation, with leave loading applied.

Health and Fitness Benefits: Access to Fitness Passport, a discounted workplace health and fitness program for you and your family, plus an annual voluntary flu vaccination to support your wellbeing.

Employee Assistance Program: Confidential counselling and support services for you and your family via our Employee Assistance Program.

Diversity and inclusion:

Statewide supports and fosters a culture in which employees feel they belong and feel safe at work. The culture aims to encourage all people to use their talents and to be valued and rewarded for their contributions.

Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander applicants are encouraged to apply. 

Application Information:

Please refer to the role description for essential educational-vocational qualifications that may be required.

Appointment will be subject to a satisfactory Criminal History Check and compliant Immunisation screening as indicated in the role description.

SA Health Services are required to implement the Addressing vaccine preventable disease: Occupational assessment, screening and vaccination policy in the workplace.

Please note that unsolicited applications from recruitment agencies or third parties will not be accepted for this position.

result.description:
CHE QLD is seeking to employ experienced MACHINIST to join our team of dedicated professionals. We are looking for hardworking individuals who can meet company challenges and surpass client expectations.

The role includes but is not limited to:
Read and interpret blueprints and technical specifications to understand the requirements for the metal component to be machined
Cut and shape custom mounting brackets, frames, and suspension components that hold truck bodies securely to vehicle chassis
Diagnose equipment malfunctions, perform repairs, and execute corrective maintenance to prevent operational disruptions
Machine and thread components for hydraulic rams, cylinder barrels, and fluid power lines that lift heavy truck bodies
Repair, fabricate, and fit heavy metal components
Operate manual and CNC machine tools, and line boring or reconditioning worn parts
Inspect broken or worn machinery parts to determine if they can be repaired or must be re-machined
Cleaning, oiling, and performing daily operational checks on workshop lathes, milling machines, and portable line-boring rigs
Relevant Mechanical Trade (essential)
Previous experience in the machining of hydraulics (desirable)
